channel.description: The FOX News Rundown is your daily news podcast for making sense of the big issues directly impacting your life. Go beyond the headlines every morning and join some of FOX News’ most exceptional journalists—including FOX News Channel reporters Peter Doocy, Aishah Hasnie, Bill Melugin, Alex Hogan, Lucas Tomlinson and Jacqui Heinrich and FOX News Radio reporters Dave Anthony, Jessica Rosenthal, Lisa Brady, and Gurnal Scott - as they tap into the global reporting resources of FOX News and get unparalleled political analysis and exclusive insight from top newsmakers. The Rundown offers a sharp contrast of perspectives you won’t hear anywhere else, and a daily commentary you can't miss, we deliver the full picture of the day's biggest events.

item.title: Questions Swirl Around NVIDIA as President Trump Heads to Asia
item.description:
President Trump has left for Asia but the questions surrounding Nvidia and how its chips ended up in China are sure to follow him as he prepares to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later this week. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is said to be joining the president on the trip, who is facing pressure from lawmakers and within the administration about why his department didn’t more aggressively clamp down on Nvidia chip exports and why the Singapore-based data center builder Megaspeed wasn’t blacklisted.
FOX's Eben Brown speaks with Max Meizlish, the deputy director of the Center on Economic and Financial Power (CEFP) at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), who says the United States has all the tools to apply pressure on China and should not be afraid to use them.

item.title: After a Slew of Tech, Aviation & Espionage Scares, How Safe Is the U.S.?
item.description:
Following a week marked by a reported Chinese espionage plot targeting Nvidia’s CEO, a massive Microsoft outage, and a rare nationwide FAA ground stop, former National Security Council senior director Michael Allen joins the Rundown to discuss concerns about America’s vulnerabilities. Allen discusses China’s use of “honeypot” tactics to target U.S. tech leaders, outdated government infrastructure and growing cyber threats. Plus, he weighs in on potential Iranian retaliation against American officials and the security challenges surrounding President Trump’s upcoming overseas travel.
Strength, hope, and faith are front and center in a new book, titled Graceful Warrior: The True Story of a Son, Father, and a Family Who Carried Each Other Through. Author, award-winning actor and advocate Gary Sinise joins the Rundown to reflect on his son Mac’s five-and-a-half year battle with chordoma, a rare and incurable form of cancer. Sinise shares what it was like serving as the primary caregiver and how decades of working with wounded veterans and military families through the Gary Sinise Foundation helped prepare him to lead his own family through unimaginable hardship.
PLUS, commentary by Jason Chaffetz, FOX News contributor and the host of the Jason In The House podcast on FOX News Radio.

item.title: 'Forever Chemicals' & Cancer Risk: What the Science Really Says
item.description:
National Cancer Institute Director Dr. Anthony Letai joined Jessica Rosenthal earlier this week on the FOX News Rundown to break down a new study examining a potential link between PFAS—'forever chemicals'—and an aggressive form of breast cancer.
Dr. Letai explains why blood levels of these chemicals have actually dropped significantly over the last two decades, shares proven ways to lower breast cancer risk, weighs in on hormone replacement therapy, and addresses the troubling rise in colorectal cancer among younger adults.
We often have to cut interviews short during the week, but we thought you might like to hear the full conversation. Today on the Fox News Rundown Extra, we will share our entire interview with Dr. Anthony Letai and let you hear more the potential risks of "forever chemicals" and other ways to both prevent and fight cancers. item.title: ‘Common Sense’: Rep. Josh Gottheimer on What Moderate Democrats Will Focus on Next Year
item.description:
Following a big midterm win, House Democrats are mapping out their plans for the new year. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) explains why Democrats need to focus on lowering everyday costs instead of far left ideas or dead-end impeachments, demands a clear White House plan for the conflict in Iran, and pushes for an investigation into whether China illegally got its hands on advanced U.S. computer chips. Plus, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis examines the midterm results as he prepares to leave office in January—arguing Republicans fell short by losing focus on the economy, while weighing in on the GOP’s path forward and his own political future.

item.title: Alleged 'Sexpionage' at NVIDIA: How 'Honeypot' Plots Work
item.description:
Reports of an alleged Chinese "honeypot" operation targeting NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang have sent shockwaves through the tech sector and Washington. The scandal even led to Huang's resignation on Thursday.
Earlier this week, former CIA station chief and Fox News contributor Dan Hoffman joined Gurnal Scott to break down how foreign intelligence services execute "sexpionage" plots, what China may have been after at the chip giant, and how the U.S. government investigates and defends American businesses against espionage and potential 'honeypot' schemes. We often have to cut interviews short during the week, but we thought you might like to hear the full interview and let you hear more of Hoffman's analysis of the NVIDA scandal and how adversaries have been targeting Americans using sex for decades.
Today on Fox News Rundown Extra, we will share our entire interview with FOX News Contributor Daniel Hoffman.

item.title: Post-Midterm Leadership Shakeups and the Pentagon Impeachment Battle
item.description:
Following a major Democratic midterm victory, both parties on Capitol Hill face high-stakes leadership battles and a crowded lame-duck agenda. Fox News Chief Congressional Correspondent Chad Pergram joins to break down Senator Chris Van Hollen’s challenge to Chuck Schumer, Hakeem Jeffries’ path to the speakership, and Jim Jordan’s election as House Minority Leader, alongside the looming December funding deadline and upcoming Nvidia hearings.
Later, a shelved House effort to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth sparks debate over partisan politics and military readiness. Medal of Honor recipient Dakota Meyer explains why targeting Hegseth undermines troop morale, details his Barracks Task Force mission to overhaul military housing, and reflects on Veterans Day.
